findings.title: Hardcoded secret: Private key material
findings.description: A PEM private key header was found in the app's strings. Private keys must never leave the server or the platform keystore.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the key pair, generate a new one, and keep private keys server-side or in the Android Keystore.

findings.title: Weak cipher algorithm: DES
findings.description: DES has a 56-bit key and can be brute-forced in hours.
findings.recommendation: Use AES-256-GCM (or ChaCha20-Poly1305) via the Android Keystore.

findings.title: ECB block-cipher mode
findings.description: ECB encrypts identical plaintext blocks to identical ciphertext blocks, leaking structure and allowing block rearrangement.
findings.recommendation: Use an authenticated mode such as AES/GCM/NoPadding with a fresh random IV for every message.

findings.title: Hardcoded encryption key
findings.description: The symmetric key is embedded in the app. Anyone can extract it from the APK and decrypt all data protected by it.
findings.evidence: SecretKeySpec built from string literal "MySu***********y1 (17 chars)"
findings.recommendation: Generate keys at runtime inside the Android Keystore; never ship key material in code or resources.

findings.title: Application is debuggable
findings.description: android:debuggable is true. Anyone with USB access can attach a debugger, run commands as the app (run-as), read its private data and bypass client-side checks.
findings.recommendation: Never ship debuggable builds. Remove the attribute; release build types set it to false by default.

findings.title: Exported provider without permission: NotesProvider
findings.description: This provider is reachable by any app on the device because android:exported is true, and no android:permission protects it. Untrusted callers can send it crafted intents. Any app can query this provider's data.
findings.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" unless external access is required; otherwise guard it with a signature-level android:permission and validate all incoming data.

findings.title: TrustManager accepts any server certificate
findings.description: checkServerTrusted() has an empty body, so TLS certificates are never validated. A network attacker can impersonate any server and read or modify supposedly encrypted traffic (man-in-the-middle).
findings.evidence: com.example.vulnapp.TrustAll implements X509TrustManager; checkServerTrusted is empty
findings.recommendation: Delete the custom TrustManager and use the platform default. To trust a private CA, add it via network_security_config.xml; to pin, use <pin-set>.

findings.title: HostnameVerifier accepts every hostname
findings.description: verify() unconditionally returns true, so a valid certificate issued for *any* domain is accepted for *every* domain, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.
findings.recommendation: Use the default HostnameVerifier (HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier()).

findings.title: WebView ignores SSL errors (handler.proceed())
findings.description: onReceivedSslError calls SslErrorHandler.proceed(), continuing to load pages that failed certificate validation. Attackers can inject content into the WebView.
findings.recommendation: Call handler.cancel() and show an error instead.

findings.title: User-installed CAs are trusted
findings.description: A <certificates src="user"> trust anchor makes the app accept certificates from CAs the device user installed, which is how interception proxies (and malware) MITM TLS.
findings.recommendation: Trust only system CAs in release builds; limit user CAs to <debug-overrides>.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret: AWS access key ID
findings.description: An AWS access key ID is embedded in the app. Anyone can extract it from the APK, and paired with the secret key it grants access to the AWS account.
findings.recommendation: Revoke and rotate the key. Never ship long-lived cloud credentials; use short-lived tokens issued by your backend (e.g. Cognito / STS).

findings.title: Hardcoded secret: GitHub token
findings.description: A GitHub personal access or OAuth token is embedded in the app.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the token at github.com/settings/tokens and rotate it.

findings.title: Cipher "AES" without mode defaults to ECB
findings.description: Cipher.getInstance("AES") falls back to AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding on Android's providers, which is not semantically secure.
findings.recommendation: Always specify the full transformation, e.g. "AES/GCM/NoPadding".

findings.title: Weak hash function: MD5
findings.description: MD5 is collision-prone and unsuitable for passwords, signatures or integrity checks. (Harmless for non-security checksums.)
findings.recommendation: Use SHA-256 or stronger; for passwords use PBKDF2/Argon2/bcrypt.

findings.title: Weak hash function: SHA-1
findings.description: SHA-1 is collision-prone and unsuitable for passwords, signatures or integrity checks. (Harmless for non-security checksums.)
findings.recommendation: Use SHA-256 or stronger; for passwords use PBKDF2/Argon2/bcrypt.

findings.title: Static (hardcoded) IV / nonce
findings.description: A constant IV makes encryption deterministic: identical plaintexts yield identical ciphertexts, and with GCM, nonce reuse reveals the key stream and breaks authentication.
findings.evidence: IV derived from string literal "0123**********ef (16 chars)"
findings.recommendation: Generate a fresh random IV per message with SecureRandom (or let Cipher.init pick it) and store it alongside the ciphertext.

findings.title: Predictable random number generator (java.util.Random)
findings.description: java.util.Random / Math.random are not cryptographically secure: their output can be predicted from a few samples. Fine for game logic, dangerous for tokens, keys, salts or IVs.
findings.recommendation: Use java.security.SecureRandom for anything security-related.

findings.title: App data can be extracted with adb backup
findings.description: With backup enabled, app-private files (databases, shared preferences, tokens) can be copied off the device via 'adb backup' or cloud backup, defeating the app sandbox.
findings.recommendation: Set android:allowBackup="false", or define precise android:dataExtractionRules / fullBackupContent exclusions for sensitive files.

findings.title: Cleartext (HTTP) traffic explicitly allowed
findings.description: android:usesCleartextTraffic is true, so the app may send data over unencrypted HTTP where an on-path attacker can read or modify it.
findings.recommendation: Use HTTPS everywhere and set usesCleartextTraffic to false, or restrict exceptions in network_security_config.xml.

findings.title: Low minSdkVersion (15)
findings.description: The app installs on old Android releases that lack modern platform security fixes and protections (e.g. TLS 1.2 defaults, network security config, runtime permissions).
findings.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to at least 24.

findings.title: Exported activity without permission: PaymentActivity
findings.description: This activity is reachable by any app on the device because android:exported is true, and no android:permission protects it. Untrusted callers can send it crafted intents.
findings.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" unless external access is required; otherwise guard it with a signature-level android:permission and validate all incoming data.

findings.title: Exported service without permission: SyncService
findings.description: This service is reachable by any app on the device because android:exported is true, and no android:permission protects it. Untrusted callers can send it crafted intents.
findings.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" unless external access is required; otherwise guard it with a signature-level android:permission and validate all incoming data.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: READ_SMS
findings.description: Can read or send SMS, a common vector for OTP theft and premium-rate fraud. Request only what the app needs and justify it in the privacy policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the permission if unused; request dangerous permissions at runtime, in context.

findings.title: Cleartext traffic permitted for all domains
findings.description: <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"> allows plain HTTP to every domain.
findings.recommendation: Set cleartextTrafficPermitted to false and use HTTPS.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret: Google API key
findings.description: A Google API key is embedded in the app. Such keys are often meant to be public (Maps, Firebase) but are abusable and billable if not restricted.
findings.recommendation: In Google Cloud Console restrict the key to your app's package name and SHA-1 fingerprint and to only the APIs it needs.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret: JSON Web Token
findings.description: A hardcoded JWT is present. If it is a real, unexpired token it lets anyone act as its subject; even expired tokens leak claims.
findings.recommendation: Remove the token and issue tokens at login. Decode it to check for sensitive claims.

findings.title: Outdated targetSdkVersion (28)
findings.description: Targeting an old API level opts the app out of newer platform hardening (scoped storage, implicit-export rules, background limits).
findings.recommendation: Target API 30 or newer.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: CAMERA
findings.description: Captures camera or microphone input; verify it is needed and user-visible. Request only what the app needs and justify it in the privacy policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the permission if unused; request dangerous permissions at runtime, in context.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
findings.description: Collects the user's location. Request only what the app needs and justify it in the privacy policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the permission if unused; request dangerous permissions at runtime, in context.

findings.title: Sensitive permission requested: WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE
findings.description: Shared storage is readable by other apps; never put secrets there. Request only what the app needs and justify it in the privacy policy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the permission if unused; request dangerous permissions at runtime, in context.

findings.title: Cleartext traffic permitted for legacy.example.com
findings.description: A <domain-config> opts specific domains into plain HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Migrate these hosts to HTTPS and remove the exception.

findings.title: No certificate pinning detected
findings.description: Neither a <pin-set> in the network security config nor a known pinning library (OkHttp CertificatePinner, TrustKit) was found. Without pinning a rogue or compromised CA can intercept traffic to your backend.
findings.recommendation: For apps handling sensitive data, pin your backend's public key (<pin-set>) and include a backup pin.
